name: disclosure
pattern: A disclosure using native details/summary, with accordion grouping through the name attribute
responsibility: Detects native details opening/closing and provides user events, state outputs, and semantic HTML validation only. Does not generate appearance or content.

targets.trigger: Exactly one native <summary> with data-disclosure-target="trigger" inside the root
targets.panel: Exactly one non-summary content container with data-disclosure-target="panel" inside the root

authorMarkup.label: Use native summary text content or a consumer-supplied accessible name.
authorMarkup.validity: Valid markup uses a native details root, a direct-child native summary trigger, and a non-summary descendant panel.
authorMarkup.accordion: Native details elements sharing a name form an accordion group through browser exclusivity. The controller neither changes name nor implements exclusivity. Report grouping guarantees as unverified in engines without name support.
authorMarkup.content: The controller does not generate elements or content.

semanticElements: The root must be an HTMLDetailsElement.
The trigger must be a native summary directly beneath the root.
The panel must be a root descendant distinct from the trigger.
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: Validate semanticElements on connection and target replacement. Invalid markup prevents listeners, ARIA, and open/state operations and warns once per root per connection. Do not throw.
contractValidation.warning: Warnings identify the controller and element types violating the contract. Revalidate when corrected markup reconnects.

open.description: Initial open state. Prefer the native open attribute; use the value only when that attribute is absent.
Current native details.open. Assignment changes native open without events or focus movement.

show().description: Open through native details.open=true without custom events or focus movement.

hide().description: Close through native details.open=false without custom events or focus movement.

toggle().description: Toggle native details.open without custom events or focus movement.

disclosure:beforetoggle.when: Before opening/closing through trusted trigger activation

detail.open: The open-and-close state about to be committed
detail.previousOpen: The open-and-close state before the change

disclosure:beforetoggle.effect: On preventDefault(), leave the panel, ARIA, and state outputs unchanged.

disclosure:toggle.when: After opening/closing through trusted trigger activation is committed

detail.previousOpen: The open-and-close state before the change

events.programmatic: open assignment, show(), hide(), toggle(), initialization, reconnection, and dynamic-target synchronization emit no events.
events.sameState: Do not emit beforetoggle/toggle for requests leaving the current open/closed state unchanged.
events.synthetic: Treat clicks with isTrusted=false as programmatic operations: toggle state without events.
events.nativeGap: Measured native details behavior in Chromium 151, Firefox 153, and WebKit 26.5 emits no beforetoggle and a noncancelable toggle. Popover beforetoggle is cancelable in all three engines in the same measurements, serving as a detector control. Only this controller supplies a cancelable event before changing disclosure state.

consumerIntegration.stimulusActions: Consumers may use data-action="disclosure:toggle->controller#method" on the root or an ancestor, and ordinary summary click actions. The controller does not stop propagation.
consumerIntegration.programmatic: Other controllers may call open/show/hide/toggle through a Stimulus controller reference or outlets. Programmatic API calls emit no events.
consumerIntegration.nested: Use the data-action :self modifier or event.target === event.currentTarget to restrict events to the owning root when listening outside nested disclosures.

behavior.initial: Prefer native details.open when authored; otherwise initialize native open from the open value. Leave panel visibility and summary keyboard behavior to the browser and synchronize data-state only.
behavior.pointer: A trusted click on an enabled summary dispatches beforetoggle with reason="pointer" before toggling native open.
behavior.keyboard: Native summary Enter/Space activation toggles through browser-generated trusted click/toggle. Do not add custom keydown activation.
behavior.disabled: Summary has no native disabled state. Treat authored disabled or aria-disabled="true" as an activation no-op. Public API changes remain allowed regardless of disabled state.
behavior.focus: Preserve native summary focus after opening/closing; do not move focus into the panel.

managedMarkup.nativeSemantics: Use native details/summary implicit roles, open state, and keyboard behavior. Do not add role, aria-expanded, aria-controls, or hidden.
managedMarkup.stateOnly: Manage only root/trigger/panel data-state. Preserve authored IDs, ARIA, open, and name attributes.
managedMarkup.preservation: Preserve authored id, open, name, role, ARIA, and other attributes. Synchronize native semantics and data-state.
managedMarkup.disabled: Read summary aria-disabled="true" or disabled as activation guards. Do not add disabled data-* attributes.

stateOutputs.ownership: Only root/trigger/panel data-state is controller-owned. HTMLDetailsElement owns native open and visibility.
stateOutputs.cssAlternative: CSS can read the root through details[open] and the trigger through details[open] > summary. Panel data-state cannot be replaced precisely by a descendant selector: with nested details, details[open] also matches panels in closed inner details.

lifecycle: Register trigger click and root toggle in connect(); remove them in disconnect(). Do not duplicate listeners on reconnection.
Leave generated attributes and state outputs in place on disconnect().
Synchronize state outputs with current markup and open value on reconnection.
Track trigger/panel additions and removals through Stimulus TargetConnected/TargetDisconnected.
Do not throw when a target is temporarily absent.

observations.environment: macOS Safari + VoiceOver and browsers with differing details/summary support
observations.item: Open/closed announcements, summary descendant role mapping, and named details grouping support
observations.impact: Native disclosure and name-based grouping remain browser-owned; these observations do not introduce custom exclusivity or role overrides.

acceptanceCriteria: Required AAA criteria: 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception), with no pointer-only features; and 3.2.5 Change on Request, with controller focus movement limited to user actions or consumer JS calls, never timers.
Conforming native details/summary and content panels must provide role, name, open state, keyboard behavior, and visibility consistent with WCAG 2.2 Level AA and the APG Disclosure Pattern.
Only trusted activation emits one cancelable beforetoggle followed by one committed toggle, in that order.
Canceling beforetoggle leaves open state, ARIA, and state outputs unchanged.
Public API calls, initialization, reconnection, and dynamic targets synchronize native open/data-state without events.
Preserve authored id, ARIA, open, and name, without adding role, aria-expanded, aria-controls, or hidden that duplicate native semantics.
Enter and Space operate the trigger; focus remains there after opening/closing.
Do not implement accordion exclusivity or keyboard movement between headings; keep responsibility limited to one disclosure.
Pass automated tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.
Report macOS Safari and VoiceOver real-device results as unverified when not performed.
The engine exhibiting summary's implicit button role while suppressing descendant roles has not been identified; report that behavior as unverified.

testMatrix.description: Valid native markup, target counts, native semantics, accessible names, authored attributes, data-state, and visibility
Initial open state preferring the open attribute over the open value
show/hide/toggle and open assignment, with no programmatic events
Synthetic-click state changes without custom events
No-op activation for disabled or aria-disabled triggers
Trusted pointer beforetoggle cancellation, toggle detail, bubbling, and order
Native Enter/Space keyboard reason and trigger focus
Panel visibility and data-state synchronized with native open
Dynamic target replacement and state synchronization
Semantic-target validation, warnings, and disabled enhancement
Preservation of authored name, role, ARIA, IDs, and other attributes

testMatrix: Engine-specific results for Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
Real-device macOS Safari and VoiceOver results

mutation.description: Disable semantic validation and enhance invalid roots.

negativeControls.expectedFailure: disclosure-semantic-validation-negative and disclosure-dynamic-targets fail on the shared disabled-enhancement invariant.
disclosure-root-state-negative, disclosure-beforetoggle-cancel, disclosure-programmatic-silence, disclosure-dynamic-targets, and disclosure-disconnect-cleanup fail on shared root state output.
disclosure-panel-state-negative and disclosure-dynamic-targets fail on shared panel state output.

mutation.description: Remove the guard preferring authored open attributes.
Emit custom events from native toggle without a pending user toggle.

negativeControls.expectedFailure: disclosure-pending-toggle-guard-negative, disclosure-synthetic-silence, disclosure-disabled-guard, and disclosure-click-trusted-negative fail on the shared pending-toggle event invariant.

mutation.description: Remove the guard preventing synthetic clicks from being treated as user activation.
Remove the synthetic-event guard from keydown.
Remove the allowed-key filter for summary keyboard activation.
Remove both disconnected inactive state and root-listener cleanup.
